identification: Folio 'Etudes de A. Calame' (Alexandre Calame, Swiss, 1810-1864) with two loose tinted lithograph landscape studies (one signed in the stone), an etching of a gnarled tree with pencil inscription, a large Victorian architectural print (multi-storey corner building, royal arms) and a Mercury (Hobart) Apollo 11 issue, July 1969. Calame lithographs are genuine 19th century but loose and foxed; the Calame lithographic studies were issued in numbers, so individual plates are modest. Mixed bag.

viewing_check: Open the folio: read the publisher imprint and date on the cover and count the plates (a complete suite is worth more than loose sheets). Photograph the stone signature and printer line on the two lithographs, the pencil inscription under the tree etching (dedication or artist signature), and the title and publisher line under the architectural print. Check the Mercury date and that it is complete (all pages) for the Apollo 11 issue.
